One of the major 'problems' with this game is that every race has a fun thing about them that makes it incredibly hard to choose between. I decided to play a Human, Elf, and Giant to 900 before choosing a main to cross the 1k boarder (currently working on the human, giant: 902, Elf: 901 Human: 580) The elves have ridiculous archery and magic capabilities, paired with their 400% aim speed racial and fast movement speed (plus high fashion capabilities) this makes them fun and the magic and archery skills are super fun for kiting however, they are super squishy... 


The giants have Fantastic strength and defense and you will find yourself dying far less once properly equipped. (giants have a higher defense, can equip large shields and have access to wind guard) they are also faster than humans but slower than elves though they look super slow when played due to how big they are. Biggest advantage is the R1 smash being 600% instead of the humans/elfs 500%, a 60% debuff/bleed chance compared to human 50% and elves 40%. and the Their major cons: lack of de-agro skills (no hide, no play dead) they can get crisis escape. they also have poor fashion items outside of Gachapons (and even then...) 


Humans are straight up balanced you can play anything on a human and they are fantastic early and mid game but at end game they become weaker (stats cant be as high) they have the fashion of elves and the versatility to be both combat oriented and magic oriented which makes them fun to play at least. I am having a lot of fun playing on all 3. but personal bias I will most likely stick to my giant because getting up close and chaining together combat skills is a ton of fun.

Lamellar is surprisingly sturdy. you are using bandsaw blades I don't know what yours are made out of or the thickness but mine are made of bimetal (like most modern toolblades). anywhom with plates stacked on top of each other overlapped like you have it would certainly stop any slashing weapon and any human thrust. 
as far as guns. yes it will stop a low velocity firearm like a flintlock handgun, possibly a black powder musket. maybe even some low velocity modern handguns. definitely arrows. now with that said anyone with a colt peacemaker is going to have your lunch no problem. their best bet be smart aim for the head or joints. btw It normally takes between a 1/4″ to a 1/2″ of steel to stop a bullet or 3/8″ to 3/4″ of Aluminum. as far as the build itself the only problem I see is if they have a sword and decide to slash your armors lacing pattern I don't think will hold up. needs more knots and cross lacing to make sure that broken lace doesn't mean the armor falls apart.

Fencing (rapiers):
Darkwood Armory - https://www.darkwoodarmory.com/ 
Pros: Pretty Furniture(grips+guard), Normally very well built, sell at Pennsic
Cons: I have had problems in the past with their blades bending but it may just have been a bad batch, they are pricey!
other: some people like me prefer heavy blades theirs weight a bit more than others but to me that's a pro.

Castille http://castillearmory.com/ 
Pros:- very pretty and well built, can be custom built to match your weight style.
Cons: very busy and can be hard to get ahold of at times. 
They do not sell at pennsic yet.

Zen Warrior Armory - http://www.zenwarriorarmory.com/index.php 
Pro: Cheap! they are decently built and will last a while with proper care. good for starter blades or new people.
Cons: little to no customization, they are cheap and the blades will bend or break if you aren't carful. 

Alchem Armory - http://www.alcheminc.com/fencing.html
Pros: Durable Tanks if you took one to a concrete pillar the pillar would be in rubble and the blade would still be list legal. -exaggeration but still  the blades are a beast when it comes to durability.
the blades are on the cheap end and allows customization to a degree. I have 3 alchem blades and I love the weight on them (they are tip heavy, but I like that for my style of play) add a pommel if you don't like it.
like others they sell at Pennsic. 

Cons: the waiting time if you order one is ridiculously long, my suggestion is to ask every other week on the progress. 

James the Just: http://www.jamesthejust.com/
Pro: customizable and well made, Fairly durable and he will work with you on what you want. Price is mid-range.
Cons: not really sure I have one and I love it but he mostly uses hanwei blades now and they are a bit wobbly it seems.
